Did you know? A battery stores energy and gives it out as electricity.
Did you know? A big gear turns slowly but pushes very hard.
Did you know? A bike has gears. Small gears help you go fast, big ones help you climb hills.
Did you know? A bug is a mistake in a program. Fixing it is called debugging!
Did you know? A doorknob is a wheel and axle!
Did you know? A drawbridge on a castle could be pulled up to keep enemies out.
Did you know? A fan uses a motor: a magnet and wire that spin when power flows.
Did you know? A flashlight is a tiny circuit: a battery, a switch and a bulb.
Did you know? A pizza cutter is a wheel with a sharp edge.
Did you know? A ramp makes it easier to move heavy things up high. The Egyptians may have used ramps to build the pyramids!
Did you know? A robot arm in space helps astronauts move big things.
Did you know? A Rube Goldberg machine does a simple job in lots of funny steps!
Did you know? A screw is really a ramp wrapped around a pole.
Did you know? A seesaw on the playground is a lever!
Did you know? A slide at the park is a ramp. Wheee!
Did you know? A wheelbarrow uses a wheel AND a lever!
Did you know? A zipper uses tiny wedges to open and close.
Did you know? An axe and a knife are wedges. Their sharp edges push things apart.
Did you know? Architects draw plans called blueprints before building starts.
Did you know? Army ants can hold on to each other to make a bridge with their own bodies.
Did you know? Big bridges have special joints that let them stretch and shrink without cracking.
Did you know? Big trucks beep when they back up, so people know to stay away.
Did you know? Big windmills called wind turbines turn wind into electricity.
Did you know? Birds can sit on a power line safely because the power does not go through them.
Did you know? Bricks are made of clay baked in a very hot oven.
Did you know? Bridge builders use triangles because a triangle can not change its shape.
Did you know? Bridges that hang from big cables are called suspension bridges.
Did you know? Builders wear hard hats to keep their heads safe.
Did you know? Bulldozers roll on tracks, so they don't sink in soft mud.
Did you know? Clocks use lots of tiny gears to move their hands.
Did you know? Coders give their programs instructions in an exact order.
Did you know? Coders test their programs again and again to find bugs.
Did you know? Coders try to use as few steps as they can. Short programs are easier to fix!
Did you know? Concrete keeps getting harder for weeks after it is poured.
Did you know? Conveyor belts carry bags at the airport.
Did you know? Copper is used in wires because electricity flows through it easily.
Did you know? Covered bridges have a roof so rain and snow do not rot the wooden road.
Did you know? Crane drivers sit in a tiny cabin high up in the sky.
Did you know? Cranes use pulleys to lift things as heavy as a whale!
Did you know? Dominoes falling one after another are a chain reaction!
Did you know? Dump trucks can tip their back up to pour out dirt and rocks.
Did you know? Electric cars run on giant batteries instead of gas.
Did you know? Electric eels can make their own electricity to zap their food!
Did you know? Electricity moves through wires super fast almost as fast as light!
Did you know? Elevators go up and down with pulleys and strong ropes.
Did you know? Engineers call ramps, levers, wedges, pulleys, wheels and screws simple machines.
Did you know? Engineers draw circuits as maps with little symbols, called circuit diagrams.
Did you know? Engineers erase and redraw their plans many times before a bridge is built.
Did you know? Engineers test robots again and again to make them better.
Did you know? Engineers test small bridge models in wind tunnels before they build the real one.
Did you know? Every app you use started with someone writing code.
Did you know? Factory robots can build cars all day without getting tired.
Did you know? Fireflies make their own light, and they do it without any electricity!
Did you know? Flagpoles use a pulley to raise the flag to the top.
Did you know? Gears that touch always turn in opposite directions.
Did you know? Hydro dams make electricity from rushing water.
Did you know? In India, some bridges are made of living tree roots that grow stronger every year.
Did you know? In Peru, people weave a rope bridge out of grass. They make a new one every year!
Did you know? LED lights use much less power than old light bulbs.
Did you know? Lightning is a giant spark of electricity in the sky!
Did you know? Long ago, a real moth got stuck inside a computer. People called it a bug!
Did you know? Loops help programmers write less and do more!
Did you know? Lots of robots have a computer inside that works like a tiny brain.
Did you know? Maze robots can find their way by following a wall.
Did you know? Most houses stand on a foundation made of concrete.
Did you know? Never put anything in a wall socket real electricity is strong and dangerous!
Did you know? Old windmills used big wooden gears to grind wheat into flour.
Did you know? People in ancient Rome built stone arch bridges. Some are still used today, 2000 years later!
Did you know? Plastic and rubber stop electricity. That is why wires have a plastic coat.
Did you know? Potholes start when water gets into little cracks in the road.
Did you know? Roads are built in layers, like a giant cake!
Did you know? Robot dogs can walk on four legs and climb stairs.
Did you know? Robots can help doctors with very careful work.
Did you know? Robots follow programs step by step, just like Robo!
Did you know? Robots on Mars drive themselves around rocks.
Did you know? Scissors are two levers stuck together.
Did you know? Self-driving cars use cameras to see the road.
Did you know? Ski lifts use pulleys and a long moving cable.
Did you know? Solar panels turn sunlight into electricity.
Did you know? Some bridges are built just for animals, so they can cross busy roads safely.
Did you know? Some bridges can swing to the side to let tall boats go by.
Did you know? Some bridges float on top of the water on big hollow blocks.
Did you know? Some bulldozers are heavier than 20 elephants!
Did you know? Some electric trains get their power from a wire above the track.
Did you know? Some factories have belts longer than a soccer field.
Did you know? Some farm robots help pick fruit and water plants.
Did you know? Some lights in a hallway can be switched on and off from two different places!
Did you know? Some robot vacuums use sensors to check for walls, like your If wall block.
Did you know? Some robots are smaller than a grain of rice!
Did you know? Some robots can swim deep in the ocean to explore.
Did you know? Some robots deliver food and packages right to your door!
Did you know? Some tower cranes can make themselves taller, one piece at a time!
Did you know? Static electricity is why a balloon rubbed on your hair can stick to a wall!
Did you know? Steel beams hold up tall buildings like a skeleton.
Did you know? Steel bridges get a tiny bit longer on hot days and shorter on cold days.
Did you know? Street lights turn on by themselves when it gets dark outside.
Did you know? Supermarket checkouts have a little belt that carries your food.
Did you know? The big flat shovel on a bulldozer is called a blade.
Did you know? The Eiffel Tower is made of iron triangles, just like a truss bridge.
Did you know? The first computer programmer was a woman named Ada Lovelace, almost 200 years ago!
Did you know? The Golden Gate Bridge has two main cables made of about 27,000 thin wires each.
Did you know? The Golden Gate Bridge in San Francisco is painted a color called International Orange.
Did you know? The light switch in your room opens and closes a circuit, just like in the game.
Did you know? The longest bridge in the world is in China. It is about 100 miles long!
Did you know? The Millau Viaduct in France is taller than the Eiffel Tower!
Did you know? The Rialto Bridge in Venice is over 400 years old and has little shops on it!
Did you know? The Sydney Harbour Bridge is called The Coat Hanger because of its arch shape.
Did you know? The tallest building in the world is taller than 2,700 feet!
Did you know? The towers of one big bridge in New York lean apart a tiny bit, because the Earth is round!
Did you know? The very first bridges were probably fallen trees lying across a stream.
Did you know? The wheel was invented about 5,000 years ago.
Did you know? The word electricity comes from an old Greek word for amber, a shiny stone.
Did you know? There is often more than one way to write a program that works.
Did you know? Thomas Edison made a light bulb that could glow for many hours.
Did you know? Tower Bridge in London can lift up its road so tall ships can sail through.
Did you know? Tower cranes can lift loads as heavy as several cars.
Did you know? Toy cars, robots and drones all use little electric motors.
Did you know? Traffic lights use simple programs to change colors.
Did you know? Triangles are used in roofs and bridges because they are so strong.
Did you know? Venice in Italy has about 400 bridges over its water streets!
Did you know? Video games are made of code lots and lots of it!
Did you know? Wheelchair ramps help people roll into buildings.
Did you know? When the Brooklyn Bridge opened, 21 elephants walked across to show it was strong!
Did you know? You are a coder now! Every coder started as a beginner, just like you.
Did you know? Your body uses tiny bits of electricity to send messages from your brain.
Did you know? Your front teeth are wedges too! They help you bite food.
Did you know? Your home has many circuits in parallel, so one light can be off while others stay on.
Did you know? Your phone runs millions of tiny instructions every second!
Did you know? Your TV remote, your toys and your watch can all run on batteries.
